stem: Which metal compound is used for the treatment of carcinoma?
expl: Carcinoma is a cancer that arises from the lining (epithelial tissue) of the skin or internal organs. Platinum-based compounds (mainly cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin) are widely used chemotherapy drugs for the treatment of carcinoma and many other solid tumours.

stem: The purest form of iron is

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The purest form of iron is wrought iron. Iron is the first element of the eighth group in the periodic table. Compared to pig iron, it is an alloy of iron with very low carbon content. Pig iron is also another form of iron, but it contains silicon, manganese, and traces of other elements; its carbon content is about 2–4%.

stem: Which of the following has highest melting point?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The melting point of a solid substance is the temperature at which it changes from the solid state to the liquid state. At the melting point, the solid and liquid phases remain in equilibrium. The melting point of boron is 2350 K, aluminium is 933.473 K, silicon is 1687 K, and iron is 1811 K. Hence, boron has the highest melting point.

stem: The chemical formula of sapphire (Ruby) is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Sapphire is a gemstone mineral. Its chemical formula is AlO. Sapphire is found in nature and can also be made 2 3 artificially. Note that sapphire and ruby are different.

stem: Which of the following corundum and cryolite are important ores ?
expl: Ore Chemical Formula Bauxite AlO·2HO Cryolite NaAlF Corundum AlO Diaspore AlO(OH) Both corundum and cryolite are ores of aluminium metal. Bauxite and diaspore are other major ores of aluminium.

stem: Gases used in welding are :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Gas welding is a process in which metals are melted and joined or repaired through heat produced by the reaction of acetylene and oxygen. Oxy-acetylene welding is the most commonly used method.

stem: Why oil is not stored in galvanized iron pot?
expl: Galvanized iron is iron coated with a layer of zinc (Zn) to protect it from rusting. The zinc layer reacts with free fatty acids and moisture present in oil and forms toxic zinc compounds. Zinc salts and metal ions increase the rate of oxidation (rancidity) of oil, thereby reducing its quality. Due to these reactions, the protective zinc layer gradually gets corroded, and the iron underneath comes in contact with moisture and oxygen; as a result, corrosion and rust are clearly observed. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

stem: Galvanized iron pipes have a coating of :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The method of protecting iron and steel from rust by coating them with a thin layer of zinc is called galvanization.

stem: the element(s) that are excreted through human sweat is/are-

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Sweat mainly consists of water; however, it also contains minerals, acids, and urea. Sweat contains elements such as sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, zinc, iron, etc. Hence, option (e) is the required answer.

stem: Which one of the following is a non-ferrous metallic mineral?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: A non-ferrous metallic mineral is a mineral that does not contain iron; for example—cobalt, tin, copper, zinc, etc. All minerals that contain iron are called ferrous metallic minerals; for example—manganese, nickel, chromium, etc.

stem: What is the glass used in tube lights and test tubes made of?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The glass used in tube lights and test tubes is an amorphous, transparent mixture of alkali metal silicates. It is prepared from silica, cerium oxide, sodium oxide, and other oxides.

stem: Which of the following metals has the highest electrical conductivity?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The order of electrical conductivity (from highest to lowest) among major metals is— Silver > Copper > Gold > Aluminium > Beryllium > Calcium.

stem: the heaviest metal among the following is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Here, “heaviest” means “density”. Among the given options, platinum (Pt) has the highest density, about 21.45 g/cm³. Silver (Ag) has a density of about 10.5 g/cm³, mercury (Hg) about 13.54 g/cm³, and gold about 19.32 g/cm³.

stem: To protect broken bones, Plaster of Paris is used. It is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Gypsum, whose chemical formula is CaSO·2HO, on heating loses water molecules and forms calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CaSO . H O). This is called “Plaster of Paris”. It is also used as bandages in surgery.

stem: the formula of Plaster of Paris is-
expl: The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is CaSO . H O (calcium sulfate hemihydrate). It is formed by heating gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate). However, as per the options, it can also be written equivalently as (CaSO)·HO.

stem: minerals are-
expl: According to geologists, a “mineral” is a naturally occurring inorganic solid, having a crystalline structure.

stem: Which is the most reactive metal?
expl: Among the given options, as per the reactivity series, potassium (K) is the most reactive metal. It reacts vigorously with air and water, producing a large amount of heat. The ionization energy of potassium is lower than that of sodium because its atomic size is larger. Metals like potassium and sodium react rapidly with cold water. Their reactions are vigorous and exothermic because the released hydrogen ignites immediately. Calcium reacts with water relatively slowly. Magnesium does not react with cold water, but with hot water it produces magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Metals like aluminium, iron, and zinc do not react with cold or hot water; rather, they react with steam to produce metal oxides and hydrogen. Metals at the top of the reactivity series (K, Na, Ca, Mg, and Al) are so reactive that they are generally not found in the free state. reactivity Series: relative reactivity of metals K Potassium Na Sodium Ca Calcium Mg Magnesium Al Aluminium Zn Zinc Fe Iron Pb Lead [H] Hydrogen Cu Copper Hg Mercury Ag Silver Au Gold

stem: Which among the following is also known as white metal?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Basically, white metal is an alloy of lead and tin, or an alloy of other metals such as cadmium, bismuth, and zinc.

stem: Which of the following seeds is used in production of engineered diamonds?
expl: Graphite is used in the production of engineered diamonds. Engineered diamonds are made under conditions of high pressure, high temperature, and chemical vapor deposition

stem:
Consider the following statements with respect to noble metals:
1. Noble metals are found in pure form in nature.
2. Uranium and lead are examples of noble metals.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: A noble metal is treated as a metallic chemical element. Noble metals are found in nature in pure as well as mixed forms. Uranium and lead are not examples of noble metals.

stem: Which one of the following metals is liquid at ordinary temperature?
expl: Mercury is liquid at normal temperature. It is used in thermometers to measure temperature.

stem: Lead (Pb) is used for—
expl: Lead is a metal of bluish-gray colour. It has metallic lustre. Its atomic number in the periodic table is 82 and it is represented by the symbol Pb. Lead is used in electric cables (overhead or underground), in chemical laboratories, and in making bullets. Lead (Pb) is also used for transmission of light.

stem: radium was obtained from which mineral?
expl: Radium is obtained from pitchblende. Pitchblende is an ore of uranium, but radium is also found in it in very small amounts. The Curie couple processed pitchblende to obtain radium.

stem: After being exposed to air for a while, a layer of green basic carbonate forms on a metal; that metal is:
expl: After being kept in air for some time, a green layer of basic carbonate (copper carbonate and copper hydroxide) forms on copper. In fact, it is the result of oxidation of copper in air.

stem: iron is obtained from which of the following minerals?
expl: Iron is obtained from the ore hematite (FeO). Other major ores of iron are magnetite (FeO), limonite (FeO(OH)·nHO), and siderite (FeCO).

stem: What is untrue for bleaching powder?

options.label: a
options.text: It is more soluble in water

options.label: b
options.text: It is powder of light yellow colour

options.label: d
options.text: It releases chlorine after reaction with dilute acid

expl: Bleaching powder is a pale yellowish-white powder having the smell of chlorine. When bleaching powder is left open in air, chlorine gas slowly escapes from it. It reacts with carbon dioxide or dilute sulphuric acid or dilute hydrochloric acid to liberate chlorine gas. CaOCl + CO → CaCO + Cl CaOCl + 2HCl → CaCl + HO + Cl CaOCl + HSO → CaSO + HO + Cl

stem: the metallurgical process in which a metal is obtained in a fused state is called

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In smelting, metal is obtained at high temperature by reduction of the ore. In this process, the metal is obtained in molten (fused), mixed, or pure state.

stem: in the method of electroplating on a vessel with zinc

options.label: a
options.text: The vessel is made to be the negative pole.

options.label: b
options.text: Pure zinc is made to the positive pole.

options.label: c
options.text: The vessel is made negative pole and pure zinc as positive pole.

options.label: d
options.text: The pot is made the positive pole and zinc the negative pole.

expl: In electroplating a vessel with zinc, zinc becomes a cation by losing two electrons, and the vessel becomes negative by gaining electrons. Thus, zinc becomes the positive electrode and the vessel becomes the negative electrode.

stem: What happens to the weight of iron, when it rusts?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: When iron rusts, it gets oxidized into hydrated iron oxide (Fe O ·nH O). Due to the addition of oxygen during 2 3 2 oxidation, the weight of iron increases; but after a long time, due to rusting, the process of iron getting consumed starts. Because of this, the weight of iron will decrease. The Bihar Public Service Commission, in its final answer key, considered option (a) as the answer.

stem: Zinc Oxide is normally used in the manufacture of

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Zinc oxide is an inorganic compound used in many manufacturing processes. It is used in rubber, plastic, ceramics, glass, cement, paints, ointments, food products, batteries, etc. It is also used secondarily in the manufacture of solvents and explosives.

stem: the heaviest metal among the following is-
expl: Among the given options, uranium is the heaviest metal. Its atomic number is 92 and its atomic mass is 238.029 u.

stem: Which of the following methods is suitable to prevent an iron frying pan from rusting?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: To prevent an iron frying pan from rusting, a zinc coating is applied. This process is called galvanisation. Zinc is more reactive than iron; therefore, it protects iron from rusting.

stem: What is manganese used for?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The major manganese ore producing states in India are Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. It is used in the manufacture of matches, leather, photography-related materials and dry batteries.

stem: What is the common name of Calcium hydroxide?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The common name of calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)] is slaked lime. Calcium hydroxide is an inorganic compound. In solid form it appears as a white powder, and in crystalline form it is colourless.

stem: Standard electrode potential of three metals A, B and C are respectively 0.5 V, -3 V and -1.2 V. Reducing power of these metals would be
expl: The more negative the standard electrode potential of a metal, the stronger its reducing power. Therefore: Metal Standard electrode potential A 0.5 V B –3 V C –1.2 V Hence, the reducing power is: B > C > A
